The packet has no local income tax schedule, and OW-2 (https://www.oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/publications/businesses/withholding-tables/WHTables-2026.pdf) has only state tables. Secondary: countrytaxcalc.com, 'No City Income Tax' for Oklahoma City, https://www.countrytaxcalc.com/tax-guides/usa/oklahoma-city-oklahoma-tax-guide-2026/.
uncertainty: No primary source states 'there is no local income tax' outright; the conclusion rests on the absence of any local income tax in the OTC forms and on a secondary source.
designImplication: No local income tax layer for Oklahoma.

claim: Nonresidents and part-year residents file Form 511-NR. A nonresident must file if Oklahoma-source gross income is $1,000 or more. Tax is computed as if all income were Oklahoma income, using the normal schedule on the full taxable income, then multiplied by Oklahoma-source AGI divided by federal AGI. Wages for work performed in Oklahoma are Oklahoma-source. Residents are taxed on all wages wherever earned and claim a credit for tax paid to the other state on Form 511-TX. Oklahoma has no reciprocal agreements with other states (secondary source).

value.method: tax on all income x (Oklahoma AGI / federal AGI)

sourceDate: 2025 Form 511-NR packet (tax year 2025); accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: 511-NR packet: 'The Oklahoma taxable income of a part-year individual or nonresident individual shall be calculated as if all income were ... After the taxable income is calculated, it is prorated using a percentage of the AGI from Oklahoma sources divided by the AGI from all sources. This prorated tax is the Oklahoma tax.' Line 17: 'The tax base (line 16) is prorated using the AGI from Oklahoma sources divided by the AGI from all sources.' Line 19 credit: 'Complete Oklahoma Form 511-TX'. Form 511 packet: 'every nonresident with gross income from Oklahoma sources of $1,000 or more is required to file'. OW-2 exempts nonresident pay of 'not more than $300.00' per quarter from withholding. Reciprocity (secondary): https://www.paylocity.com/resources/tax-compliance/tax-facts/oklahoma/ and https://www.patriotsoftware.com/blog/payroll/tax-reciprocity-between-states-agreement/.
uncertainty: 'No reciprocity' is from secondary payroll sources; no OTC statement of it was found, but neither packet mentions any agreement. The precise Form 511-TX credit limitation formula was not extracted.
designImplication: Nonresident tax = schedule(taxable income computed on all income) x (OK-source AGI / federal AGI). For residents working elsewhere, tax all wages and subtract an other-state credit (511-TX).

claim: Employers withhold using the OTC's Packet OW-2 (2026 edition, revised 11-2025, effective January 1, 2026), by either the percentage formula or the wage-bracket tables, based on the allowances on the employee's OTC Form OK-W-4. Each allowance is worth $1,000 a year ($83.33 a month). The annual single table withholds nothing up to $10,100 of wages after allowances, then 2.5% to $11,250, $28.75 plus 3.5% to $13,550, and $109.25 plus 4.5% above that. The married table doubles those thresholds. Withholding is rounded to the whole dollar.
sourceDate: Packet OW-2, Revised 11-2025, 'Effective Date: January 1, 2026'; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: OW-2: 'The number of withholding allowances claimed on OTC Form OK-W-4 must be used'; 'withholding allowance amount is the Oklahoma individual income tax personal exemption amount of $1,000.00 divided by the number of payroll periods'; Table 7 ANNUAL single: '$10,100 $11,250 ... 2.50% of the excess over $10,100 ... $28.75 +(3.50% of the excess over $11,250) ... $109.25 +(4.50% of the excess over $13,550)'; 'Round to the nearest whole dollar'. The sample computation uses '4.5%'.
uncertainty: The table text was extracted from a PDF whose layout scrambles columns; the annual brackets were cross-checked against the raw-order extraction and against the statute (10,100 = 6,350 + 3,750). The packet text does not say what an employer does when no OK-W-4 is on file.
designImplication: Withhold per pay period: annualize (wages - allowances x $1,000), apply the 2026 annual table, de-annualize and round. This approximates the year's liability, so most single wage earners land near a zero balance.

claim: The return is due April 15 (paper) or April 20 if filed electronically. The April 20 payment date holds only if the payment is also made electronically; otherwise penalty and interest run from April 15. A weekend or holiday rolls the date to the next business day. A federal extension extends the Oklahoma filing date automatically only if no Oklahoma tax is owed; otherwise the taxpayer files Form 504-I. An extension does not extend payment: at least 90% of the tax must be paid by the original due date to avoid the late-payment penalty, and interest runs on any unpaid amount from that date.

value.federalExtensionAccepted: only if no Oklahoma liability owed

establishes: Form 511 packet: 'If you file your return electronically ... your due date is extended to April 20th. Any payment of taxes due on April 20th must be remitted electronically in order to be considered timely paid'; 'A valid extension of time ... automatically extends the due date of your Oklahoma return if no Oklahoma liability is owed ... an extension ... can be requested on Form 504-I. At least 90% of the tax liability must be paid by the original due date'. OAC 710:50-3-4 (2025 Chapter 50, https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/rules-and-policies/agency-rules/2025/Chapter_50-Income_Tax-2025.pdf) says the same, citing OTC Form 504. 68 O.S. 2375(A): 'The tax shall be deemed delinquent if unpaid after the twentieth day of April if the return is electronically filed.'
uncertainty: The length of the extension (to October 15, mirroring federal) is not quoted here. The OAC names 'Form 504' and the packet names '504-I'.
designImplication: Due date = April 15, or April 20 for e-file with e-pay. An extension moves only the filing date; with an extension and at least 90% paid on time, no late-payment penalty applies, but interest always runs on the unpaid balance from the original date.

claim: If income tax shown due is not paid by the due date, a one-time 5% penalty on the total tax due is added. It is not monthly, has no cap beyond that and no minimum found. With a valid extension the penalty does not apply if at least 90% was paid on time. The OTC drops the penalty if the taxpayer pays the tax and interest within 60 days of the mailing of a proposed assessment, or pays voluntarily with an amended return. Penalties themselves bear interest.
sourceDate: 68 O.S. § 2375(B) (text from the Oklahoma Senate's Title 68 compilation posted 2019-12); confirmed by the 2025 Form 511 packet line 41a and the OTC Pay Taxes page; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: 68 O.S. 2375(B): 'If any tax due under Section 2351 et seq. ... is not paid on or before the date such tax becomes delinquent, a penalty of five percent (5%) of the total amount of the tax due shall be added ... However, the Tax Commission shall not collect the penalty assessed if the taxpayer remits the tax and interest within sixty (60) days of the mailing of a proposed assessment'. 2375(F): these penalties 'supersede all other provisions for penalties on income taxes' (so the 10% penalty in 217(D) does not apply). Form 511 line 41a: 'compute a 5% penalty on the income tax due'. OTC Pay Taxes page: 'If at least 90% of the tax liability is not paid by the original due date ... a penalty of 5% shall be charged', https://oklahoma.gov/tax/individuals/pay-taxes.html. 68 O.S. 217(G): 'the penalties bearing interest as provided in this section'.
uncertainty: The statute text comes from a 2019 compilation; the 2025 OTC packet and web page confirm the 5% rule still applies. How the 90% safe harbor interacts with a filer who has no extension but pays 90% on time is unclear; the OTC page states it without the extension condition.
designImplication: Late payment: add 5% of the unpaid tax once, on the day after the due date (unless the extension and 90% rule is met). Forgive it if tax and interest are paid within 60 days of a proposed assessment.

claim: Oklahoma has no separate monthly late-filing penalty for individual income tax. Lateness is penalized through the one-time 5% late-payment penalty and 1.25% monthly interest on tax not paid by the due date, so a late return showing a refund or zero due draws no penalty. Separate penalties apply when the OTC must act: 25% of the assessment if the taxpayer refuses to file within 10 days of a written demand by registered letter; 10% of a deficiency due to negligence; 50% for fraud (the OTC's rules say continued failure to file may evidence fraud). These are added on top of the 5% and interest, not in place of them.

value.combination: additive with 5% late-payment penalty and interest

sourceDate: 68 O.S. § 2375(B)-(F) (Senate compilation 2019-12); OAC 710:50-3-23 (2025 Chapter 50); accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: 68 O.S. 2375(C): 'If any part of deficiency, arbitrary or jeopardy assessment ... is based upon ... the refusal of any taxpayer to file ... within ten (10) days after a written demand ... by registered letter with a return receipt attached, the Tax Commission may assess and collect, as a penalty, twenty-five percent (25%) of the amount of the assessment.' (D) negligence 10%; (E) fraud 50%. OAC 710:50-3-23(b): fraud penalty 'may result' from '(1) Continued failure to file Oklahoma Income Tax Returns'. https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/rules-and-policies/agency-rules/2025/Chapter_50-Income_Tax-2025.pdf
uncertainty: The 25% penalty is discretionary ('may'). 'No separate late-filing penalty' is inferred from 2375(F), which makes 2375 the exclusive set of income-tax penalties, and from Form 511 line 41 listing only the 5% penalty and interest; no OTC page states it in those words.
designImplication: Do not charge a per-month late-filing penalty. A late filer with tax due pays 5% + interest; ignoring an OTC demand for 10 days escalates to an additional 25% of the OTC's own assessment.

claim: Interest on unpaid income tax runs at 1.25% per month (15% a year, simple) from the original due date until paid. It accrues even when no penalty applies (for example under a valid extension), and it runs on penalties too. The rate is fixed in statute, not reset annually, so it is 1.25% a month in 2025, 2026 and 2027. Underpaid estimated tax is charged at 20% a year instead. Refunds not paid within 45 days of an e-filed return, or 90 days of a paper return, earn interest at the same 1.25% a month.
sourceDate: 68 O.S. § 217(A),(G),(H) (last amended Laws 2016, c. 28, eff. July 1, 2016; Senate compilation 2019-12); 2025 Form 511 packet line 41b; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: 68 O.S. 217(A): 'interest at the rate of one and one-quarter percent (1 1/4%) per month from the date of the delinquency until paid'; (G): 'the penalties bearing interest as provided in this section for the tax'; (H)(3): refund interest after 'forty-five (45) days' (electronic) or 'ninety (90) days' (other). Form 511 line 41b: 'Compute interest on the income tax due at 1.25% per month from the original due date'. OTC Pay Taxes: 'If less than 100% of the tax liability is paid by the original due date ... interest on the unpaid amount is assessed, even when no delinquent penalty is assessed', and estimated-tax underpayment interest at '20% per annum', https://oklahoma.gov/tax/individuals/pay-taxes.html.
uncertainty: How a partial month is counted (whole months versus a daily proration) is not stated in the sources read; 'monthly' accrual is an assumption. Whether interest is computed on accrued penalty only from assessment, or from the due date, is not specified.
designImplication: Accrue 1.25% of the outstanding tax and penalty per month (simple, no compounding on interest) from the original due date. The rate does not change by year.

claim: A voluntary partial payment is applied as the taxpayer directs in specific written instructions. Without instructions, and for every involuntary payment (from a levy, garnishment, tax warrant, or a payout agreement made after collection action), the OTC applies it in this order: tax of non-trust-fund liabilities, oldest period first; then tax of trust-fund liabilities (such as withholding or sales tax), oldest first; then interest, penalties, service charges and fees, in that order, on non-trust-fund liabilities, oldest first; then the same on trust-fund liabilities. Individual income tax is a non-trust-fund tax.

defaultOrder: interest, then penalties, then service charges, then fees (non-trust-fund, oldest first)

sourceDate: OAC 710:1-3-45 and 710:1-3-46 (added 10 Ok Reg 3819 eff 7-12-93; last amended 22 Ok Reg 1513 eff 6-11-05), 2025 Chapter 1 compilation; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: OAC 710:1-3-46(a): 'Voluntary partial payments ... will be applied ... in the manner designated by the taxpayer, where the taxpayer provides specific written instructions'; (b): 'involuntary partial payments will be allocated ... (1) First, to the tax portion of non-trust fund tax liabilities, beginning with the earliest such liability period ... (3) Next, to the interest, penalties, service charges, and fees, in that order'. 710:1-3-45: 'Payments made pursuant to an installment or "payout" agreement entered into as a result of or subsequent to the institution of any of the above collection measures are deemed involuntary payments.'
uncertainty: The order is the default 'unless the Commission determines that a different allocation will better serve the State's interests'. That income tax counts as 'non-trust fund' is an inference: trust-fund taxes are those collected from others and held in trust (withholding, sales).
designImplication: Apply undesignated payments to tax first (oldest year first), then interest, then penalty, then fees. Optionally let the player designate a voluntary payment.

claim: Collection follows a set sequence. (1) A balance-due bill (billing notice) with tax, penalty and interest goes out after the return is processed. (2) For deficiencies, the OTC mails a proposed assessment; the taxpayer has 60 days to protest under oath (extendable by up to 90 more days), or it becomes final. (3) Once the tax is delinquent the OTC may at once issue a tax warrant, filed with the county clerk, which is a lien on real property for 10 years (refileable) and is mailed to the taxpayer. The sheriff executing it is owed the greater of $15 or 10% of the amount collected, capped at $200. (4) The OTC may also garnish wages and levy bank accounts. (5) Accounts more than 90 days overdue may go to a contracted collection agency, whose fee (up to 35% of the amount collected) is added to the debt. (6) State licenses are not renewed for income-tax noncompliance, after at least 6 months' notice, unless the taxpayer is on a payment agreement. (7) Refunds are offset (see refund-offsets).

steps.step: tax warrant / lien filed with county clerk

sourceDate: 68 O.S. §§ 221, 230, 231, 238.1, 255 (Senate compilation 2019-12); OAC 710:1-3-51 (2025 Chapter 1); OTC Help Center and Tax Warrants pages; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: 68 O.S. 221(C): 'Within sixty (60) days after the mailing of the aforesaid proposed assessment, the taxpayer may file ... a written protest'; (E) otherwise it 'shall become final and absolute'; (F) extension 'not to exceed an additional ninety (90) days'. 231(A): 'If any tax ... is not paid before the same becomes delinquent, the Oklahoma Tax Commission may immediately issue a warrant'; lien released 'upon the expiration of ten (10) years'. 255(A),(E): agency for 'taxes more than ninety (90) days overdue', fees 'not in excess of thirty-five percent (35%)', which 'shall be added to the amount of the delinquent taxes'. 238.1(A),(D): 'at least six (6) months notice'; a licensee 'abiding by a payment agreement' is compliant. OAC 710:1-3-51: sheriff gets '$15.00, or ... Ten Percent ... whichever amount is greater, but not to exceed $200.00'. OTC Help Center, https://oklahoma.gov/tax/helpcenter/income-tax.html: 'You will receive a billing notice that will include the remaining tax, penalty and interest' and 'You may have a tax lien issued, your wages garnished, or your bank account levied'. Tax Warrants page, https://oklahoma.gov/tax/helpcenter/taxwarrants.html: a warrant 'becomes a public record'. OTC Pay Taxes page names the contracted agencies (Harris & Harris; Linebarger Goggan Blair & Sampson).
uncertainty: The number of days between the billing notice, any second notice and warrant filing in OTC practice was not found; the statute allows a warrant immediately upon delinquency. The contracted agencies' actual fee rate is not published; 35% is the statutory maximum. The statute text is from a 2019 compilation.
designImplication: Sequence: bill, then (for audits) a proposed assessment with a 60-day protest window, then a tax warrant/lien, then garnishment/levy and collection-agency referral after 90 days (add up to 35%). Spacing between notices is a game parameter, since Oklahoma does not publish fixed intervals.

claim: Individuals request a payment plan through OkTAP after receiving a billing notice; the OTC does not publish the individual plan terms. Secondary sources describe plans of 2 to 12 months for balances over $100, with at least $25 a month, no down payment except after a prior default (50%), and no plan once the account is with a collection agency. The only published OTC rule on installment agreements (written for businesses facing closure) sets a 12-month maximum, a 25% down payment and no plan for $500 or less, and says a tax warrant is filed to protect the State. Interest and penalty keep accruing during a plan.

value.downPayment_secondary: none, or 50% after a prior default

sourceDate: OTC Pay Taxes page and Help Center (current as accessed); OAC 710:1-5-115 (amended 35 Ok Reg 2033, eff 9-14-18); secondary taxcure.com; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: OTC Help Center: 'pay what you can with the return. You will receive a billing notice ... You can set up a payment plan on OkTAP', https://oklahoma.gov/tax/helpcenter/income-tax.html. OAC 710:1-5-115(a): 'taxpayers owing tax delinquencies of Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) or less are not eligible ... require a down payment equal to or greater than one-fourth (1/4) ... shall not exceed twelve (12) months. A tax warrant ... will be filed', https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/rules-and-policies/agency-rules/2025/Chapter_1-Administrative_Operations-2025.pdf. Secondary: https://taxcure.com/state-taxes/oklahoma/payment-plan ('you must owe more than $100'; 'two to 12 months'; 'at least $25 per month').
uncertainty: WEAK. The individual income tax plan terms (minimum balance, term, monthly minimum, down payment) are from a secondary source only. OAC 710:1-5-115 sits in the business-closure subchapter and may not govern individual income tax plans. No setup fee and no decision time were found (decisionTimeDays NOT FOUND).
designImplication: Offer an OkTAP plan of up to 12 months for balances over $100, interest continuing at 1.25% a month on the declining balance. Treat the terms as tunable parameters flagged as secondary-sourced.

claim: Under the OTC's published installment rule, missing a payment or failing to file and pay new taxes during the agreement is a default. For businesses facing closure, default triggers immediate enforcement without further notice. Payments under an agreement count as voluntary only while the taxpayer stays in full compliance. On default they become involuntary, and the OTC may apply them as it chooses and resume collection (warrant, levy, garnishment, agency referral). A licensee on a payment agreement keeps the license; one in default loses that protection. Secondary sources say three defaults end eligibility for future plans and a prior default requires a 50% down payment. No official rule on curing a default, or on adding a new balance to an existing plan, was found.

defaultTriggers: failure to file returns or pay new taxes during the term

sourceDate: OAC 710:1-5-115(b),(d) (eff 9-14-18) and 710:1-3-45 (eff 7-12-93), 2025 Chapter 1 compilation; 68 O.S. § 238.1(D); secondary taxcure.com; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: OAC 710:1-5-115(b)(3): 'Taxpayer must remain in compliance, filing all tax returns and paying in full all taxes that come due during the term'; (d): 'Taxpayers failing to abide by the requirements ... will be considered in default. Once in default, a Closure Order will be served immediately without further notice'. 710:1-3-45: agreement payments are voluntary 'only so long as the taxpayer remains in full compliance with the terms of such agreement'. 68 O.S. 238.1(D): 'A licensee who has entered into and is abiding by a payment agreement ... shall be deemed to be in compliance'. Secondary: https://taxcure.com/state-taxes/oklahoma/payment-plan ('Once you default three times over any time period, you are no longer eligible for a payment plan').
uncertainty: WEAK for individuals: the default rule quoted is in the business-closure subchapter. The cure period (curePeriodDays) and whether a new year's balance can join an existing plan (newBalanceJoinsPlan) are both NOT FOUND. Default counts and down payment after default are secondary.
designImplication: A missed payment, or a new unpaid balance during the plan, puts the plan in default with no grace period; collection resumes and payments become OTC-allocated. Treat cure and plan-merging as game design choices, not Oklahoma rules.

claim: When a required return is not filed, the OTC can assess an estimated tax based on its own determination of the taxpayer's Oklahoma taxable income, typically from IRS data, adjusting it if a return is later filed. It first serves a written demand to file; if the taxpayer refuses to file within 10 days, a 25% penalty on the assessment may be added. The assessment is issued as a proposed assessment, which the taxpayer has 60 days to protest under oath (extendable by up to 90 days); otherwise it becomes final. The 5% late-payment penalty and 1.25% monthly interest also apply. Filing a return replaces the estimate. Within one year after it becomes final, a taxpayer may still ask for abatement of a clearly erroneous assessment. The OTC's rules treat continued non-filing, or non-filing where the IRS imposed a failure-to-file penalty, as evidence of fraud (50%).

value.basis: OTC's own determination of Oklahoma taxable income (estimated)

establishes: 68 O.S. 2375(C): '...within ten (10) days after a written demand ... the Tax Commission may assess and collect, as a penalty, twenty-five percent (25%) ... the Tax Commission shall assess the tax as an estimated tax on the basis of its own determination of the Oklahoma taxable income of the taxpayer, to be adjusted if and when Oklahoma taxable income is ascertained'. 221(C): 60-day written protest; (E): final if not protested; may 'within one (1) year of the date the assessment becomes final, request the Tax Commission to adjust or abate the assessment' if 'clearly erroneous'. OAC 710:50-3-23(c): an assessment based on IRS information showing a federal failure-to-file penalty makes 'the taxpayer's failure to file ... evidence of fraud'. https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/rules-and-policies/agency-rules/2025/Chapter_50-Income_Tax-2025.pdf
uncertainty: The OTC's actual non-filer letter names, timing and how it estimates income (for example W-2 or IRS data without the standard deduction) were not found on OTC pages. Whether the 25% is applied routinely or only on refusal after a registered-letter demand is discretionary.
designImplication: A non-filer gets a demand; after 10 days the OTC issues an estimated proposed assessment (optionally +25%), with 60 days to protest or file. Filing the real return replaces the estimate.

claim: An Oklahoma refund is first applied to the taxpayer's own delinquent Oklahoma taxes, including prior-year income tax. Next come claims of at least $50 filed by state agencies, district and municipal courts, district attorneys and public housing authorities (the OTC has first priority, then DHS child and spousal support, then other claims in order received). A 5% collection expense is added (2% kept by the OTC, 3% to the claimant), and the debtor has 60 days to contest with the claimant. Refunds can also go to IRS debts. Oklahoma takes part in the federal Treasury Offset Program, so federal refunds can be offset for final Oklahoma income tax debts no more than 10 years delinquent, after a certified-mail notice giving 60 days to dispute.
sourceDate: 68 O.S. §§ 205.2, 217(H) (Senate compilation 2019-12); OAC 710:50-12-1 to 12-5 (added 22 Ok Reg 1532, eff 6-11-05), 2025 Chapter 50; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: 68 O.S. 205.2(B): a qualified entity 'seeking to collect a debt ... of at least Fifty Dollars ($50.00) ... may file a claim'; '(e) a collection expense of five percent (5%)'; (E) 'retaining two percent (2%) and transferring three percent (3%)'; (F) 'The Tax Commission shall deduct from any state tax refund ... the amount of delinquent state tax'; (G) 'The Tax Commission shall have first priority ... a claim filed by the Department of Human Services for the collection of child support and spousal support shall have priority over all other claims'. 217(H)(1) refers to refunds applied to 'a debt owed to the Internal Revenue Service ... or to a state agency'. OAC 710:50-12-1: implements 'the Treasury Offset Program, "TOP" authorized by 26 U.S.C. § 6402(e)'; 12-2: debt 'not ... delinquent for more than 10 years'; 12-4: notice 'by certified mail ... at least 60 days'. https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/resources/rules-and-policies/agency-rules/2025/Chapter_50-Income_Tax-2025.pdf. OTC Help Center explains 'snagged' refunds (OTC's own tax) versus warrant intercepts (other agencies).
uncertainty: No agreements to offset refunds for or with other states' tax agencies were found (otherStateAgreements NOT FOUND). The 205.2 text is from a 2019 compilation; claimant categories may have grown since.
designImplication: Apply a refund to own Oklahoma tax debt first, then agency claims of $50 or more (plus 5%), then release the remainder. Separately, final Oklahoma income tax debts can take the player's federal refund via TOP after 60 days' notice.

claim: The OTC says e-filers can begin checking refund status about four days after the return is accepted, and paper filers should allow four to six weeks before checking. Once processed, direct deposit takes about five business days, and a debit card or paper check five to seven business days. By statute, the OTC owes interest at 1.25% a month on an income tax refund not paid within 45 days of a complete e-filed return or 90 days of a paper one. Refunds that are offset earn no such interest.
sourceDate: 2025 Form 511 packet ('Refunds', p. 6); 68 O.S. § 217(H)(3) (applies to returns filed after Jan. 1, 2010); accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: Form 511 packet: 'If your return was e-filed, you can generally begin checking on your refund about four days after the return was accepted ... If your return was paper filed, you should allow four to six weeks to begin checking ... allow five business days for the deposit ... For debit card and paper check refunds, allow five to seven business days'. 68 O.S. 217(H)(3): interest if not paid within 'forty-five (45) days' (electronic) or 'ninety (90) days' (other), at 'the same rate specified for interest on delinquent tax payments'. https://oksenate.gov/sites/default/files/2019-12/os68.pdf
uncertainty: The OTC publishes when status checks become available, not a guaranteed processing time. The 45- and 90-day statutory points are the firmest timing anchors.
designImplication: Release an e-filed refund about 1-3 weeks after filing and a paper refund about 6-8 weeks after; if the game delays past 45/90 days, pay 1.25% a month interest.
